scores.reason: Introduces learnable polynomial coefficients for Newton-Schulz orthogonalization with experiments on efficiency and convergence; does not explicitly compare fixed vs. per-iteration schedules or address bf16 stability.
Physics experiment on muon EDM; no connection to optimization, neural networks, or Muon optimizer.
Pure mathematics on polynomial inequalities; no relevance to optimizers or neural network training.

Analyzes practical Muon with finite Newton-Schulz iterations and their convergence impact; addresses mechanism of approximation quality on optimization but does not vary coefficients or test low-precision.
Quantum optics comment; unrelated to machine learning optimization.
Explains Muon's design through surrogate quadratic model; may shed light on why Newton-Schulz works but does not compare coefficient schedules.
Convergence theory for inexact polar decomposition (including Newton-Schulz) with heavy-tailed noise; addresses mechanism of approximation error propagation but not coefficient variation.
Improves Newton-Schulz initialization and removes one iteration (5→4); addresses iteration count but does not vary polynomial coefficients or test training quality metrics directly.
Studies fractional spectral powers and bivariate recurrences; different approach from Newton-Schulz coefficient variation, not directly comparable to fixed-quintic baseline.

Directly compares cubic (3-step) vs. quintic (5-step) Newton-Schulz schedules; reports training-quality metrics across NanoGPT and MoE/Mamba experiments; probes relationship between polynomial schedule and training quality at low iteration counts.
Reduces convergence requirement for Newton-Schulz via adaptive preconditioning; addresses efficiency not coefficient schedules or training quality comparison.

Explicitly analyzes the empirically tuned coefficients (3.4445, −4.7750, 2.0315); establishes convergence for practical Muon; foundational for understanding current design, though does not compare alternative coefficient schedules.
Normalization step after orthogonalization; does not address Newton-Schulz polynomial coefficients or iteration schedules.
Spectral deflation improves Newton-Schulz efficiency by preprocessing; does not vary coefficients and focuses on approximation accuracy rather than training-quality metrics.
Periodic application of 5-step Newton-Schulz (every K steps); addresses when to orthogonalize, not coefficient variation or low-iteration low-precision effects.

Analyzes how approximation error in polar steps alters discrete-time dynamics and affects finite-time performance; addresses mechanism but on strongly convex quadratics, not training tasks or low-precision scenarios.
Hamiltonian gradient-flow perspective on Muon; theoretical framework without focus on Newton-Schulz coefficient schedules or numerical stability.
Studies representation geometry and mentions Newton-Schulz backend; does not compare coefficient schedules or address iteration-count or stability tradeoffs.
Empirical comparison of Muon vs. AdamW on matrix factorization; does not examine Newton-Schulz coefficients or approximation schedules.
Analyzes spectral dynamics and noise geometry under idealized assumptions; no coverage of Newton-Schulz polynomial design, iteration counts, or numerical stability.
